body.statement: Can a first-order arbitrary-action Gaussian oracle comparison exclude positive pilot fractions satisfying \(m/n\to c\in(0,1)\) and \(N\asymp n\)?  The handle is to combine the positive macroscopic deletion coefficient \(c a(\beta)\) with a uniform first-order lower comparison showing that a learned finite action cannot offset the oracle deletion loss.
body.justification: The positive first-order deletion cost must be compared against every possible learned main-wave action.
body.gap: The current core has no arbitrary-action Gaussian oracle comparison on a positive pilot-fraction window.
body.consumer: It rules out macroscopic pilots in the endpoint-coercivity premise.

obligation.what_is_open: A first-order Gaussian oracle lower comparison uniform over all pilot-measurable main-wave actions when the pilot fraction is positive.
obligation.obstruction: The positive macroscopic deletion loss is proved, but exact accounting permits an action-regret term whose sign relative to the full oracle cannot be controlled by the one-wave risk upper bound.
obligation.attempted: Derived the positive limit \(nD_{n,m}(\beta)\to c a(\beta)\); a uniform arbitrary-action comparison is still needed to prevent cancellation.
obligation.partial_result: The proved first-order deletion relation gives \(nD_{n,m}(\beta)\to c a(\beta)>0\).  What remains is a uniform comparison over arbitrary pilot-measurable actions ensuring that the main-wave action term cannot cancel this positive first-order loss.
